note: Claims cho lời phim (claim_en tiếng Anh; ghi chú tiếng Việt). status: XÁC MINH | CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC | MÂU THUẪN. moc = mốc đinh M1–M7; moc_index liệt kê claim XÁC MINH theo mốc.

khong_dung.ly_do: USBR: 112 gồm các ca 1922 (trước khi đập được phê duyệt) và người không chết tại công trường; số "chính thức" là 96 (industrial fatalities). Nếu nói 112 phải giải thích; mặc định dùng 96.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Workers are buried in Hoover Dam’s concrete
khong_dung.ly_do: USBR: "No one is buried in Hoover Dam."

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Lake Mead is the largest reservoir in the world
khong_dung.ly_do: Câu này xuất hiện trong Census story 2025 nhưng sai/không có cơ sở (nhiều hồ chứa lớn hơn trên thế giới); USBR chỉ mô tả dung tích. Nếu cần: "largest reservoir in the United States by capacity" — CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Las Vegas uses more water per person than anywhere
khong_dung.ly_do: Không có nguồn gốc; các chỉ số GPCD mâu thuẫn theo định nghĩa (211→89 consumptive; 314 tổng cầu 2003; 75 "net" 2013). Không so sánh xếp hạng.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Lake Mead has dropped about 160 feet since 2000
khong_dung.ly_do: SNWA vẫn ghi ~160 ft nhưng đã lỗi thời: HDB 01/01/2000 ≈ 1.214 ft (cuối 01/2000: 1.214,26) → 1.037,54 ft (14/10/2026) ≈ 177 ft. Dùng số tính từ dữ liệu, nêu ngày.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Lake Mead is at its lowest level ever
khong_dung.ly_do: Trong giai đoạn tích nước ban đầu 1935–37 mực hồ thấp hơn (HDB 02/02/1935 = 670 ft). Nói "lowest since it first filled".

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Herbert Hoover chaired the 1922 Compact negotiations
khong_dung.ly_do: Văn bản Compact chỉ ghi "negotiations participated in by Herbert Hoover appointed by The President as the representative of the United States" và "Approved: HERBERT HOOVER".

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: The Boulder Canyon Project Act gave Nevada 300,000 acre-feet
khong_dung.ly_do: BCPA chỉ "authorized" hiệp định ba bang (không thành). Phần 300.000 được Toà Tối cao xác định (1963) và ấn định trong Decree 1964.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Hoover Dam was completed and dedicated in 1936
khong_dung.ly_do: City of Las Vegas timeline ghi vậy, nhưng khánh thành 30/09/1935 (Census); hoàn tất mọi hạng mục 01/03/1936 (USBR).
City timeline; Census 1910 ghi Las Vegas precinct 945, Clark County 3.321.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: The SP,LA&SL later became the Southern Pacific
khong_dung.ly_do: USBR project page viết vậy nhưng sai — tuyến này về sau thuộc Union Pacific (City timeline: "Union Pacific’s Las Vegas Land & Water Co."). Không trích câu đó.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Nevada will lose more than 70% of its water
khong_dung.ly_do: Lập luận của Thống đốc Nevada về kịch bản tối đa của ROD; mức cắt thực tế 2027 là 50.000 af (16,7%). Chỉ dùng khi gán rõ là lời của bang trong vụ kiện.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: California's first water cut in history (2027)
khong_dung.ly_do: Chưa tìm thấy văn bản chính quyền nói "first". OG 2027–2028 ghi California giảm 440.000 af — dùng con số, bỏ chữ "first".

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Tropical Storm Rachel flooded Las Vegas on Oct 13, 2026
khong_dung.ly_do: NHC: Hurricane RACHEL (EP18); advisory cuối 11/10/2026 cho tàn dư ở 35.8N 114.6W. Ngày/thiệt hại lũ ở Las Vegas chưa có nguồn NWS — CHỜ.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Intake 3 can draw water below 875 feet
khong_dung.ly_do: SNWA chỉ nói tiếp cận nước dưới dead pool 895 ft; con số 875/860 không có trong nguồn đã tải.

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Imperial Irrigation District holds a 3.1 million acre-foot right
khong_dung.ly_do: Con số QSA chưa được trích từ nguồn gốc trong phiên này; dùng mức tiêu thụ thực 2025 (2.187.165 af, USBR).

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Nevada cut divorce residency to six weeks in 1931
khong_dung.ly_do: Đúng theo nhiều nguồn thứ cấp nhưng chưa có văn bản Statutes of Nevada 1931; chỉ nói "shortened" (City timeline).

khong_dung.su_that_pho_bien: Southern Nevada uses 75 gallons per person per day
khong_dung.ly_do: Mulroy 2013 ("net water use of 75 gpcd") — định nghĩa "net" khác với GPCD hiện hành của SNWA; mâu thuẫn, không dùng.

claims.claim_en: On May 15, 1905, the San Pedro, Los Angeles & Salt Lake Railroad auctioned off the lots of a new townsite in the desert — the day modern Las Vegas was born.
claims.nguon: City of Las Vegas, "City of Las Vegas Timeline" (CO-14073)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Las Vegas was born May 15, 1905 On this day the San Pedro, Los Angeles & Salt Lake Railroad held a land auction for Sen. Clark’s Las Vegas Townsite, 40 blocks anchored at the junction of Fremont and Main streets, marking the beginning of modern Las Vegas.
claims.ghi_chu: Toạ độ: nguồn chỉ nêu "junction of Fremont and Main streets" — không có lat/lon chính thức; toạ độ kèm theo là điểm nội suy Census của City of Las Vegas (KHÔNG phải điểm đấu giá). Số lô đấu giá: nguồn thứ cấp lệch nhau (600 vs 1.200) — không dùng.

toa_do.nguon: Census 2020 PL 94-171 geo header (internal point, Las Vegas city)

claims.claim_en: The railroad stopped here for one reason: water. Las Vegas was picked as a division point because of its springs.
claims.nguon: City of Las Vegas Timeline (CO-14073)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: In 1902, Senator William A. Clark began a railroad line to connect California and Utah, selecting Las Vegas as a division point because of its springs.

claims.claim_en: Weeks before the auction, the railroad formed the Las Vegas Land and Water Company to supply water to its locomotives and to the new town.
claims.nguon: USBR, Robert B. Griffith Water Project (project history page)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The Las Vegas Land and Water Co. was formed on May 2, 1905, to supply water to the locomotives and domestic water to the new town that was established by the railroad company.
claims.ghi_chu: Cùng đoạn USBR viết "(later the Southern Pacific Railroad)" — sai (tuyến SP,LA&SL về sau thuộc Union Pacific; City timeline nói "Union Pacific's Las Vegas Land & Water Co."). Chỉ trích câu về công ty nước.

claims.claim_en: "Las Vegas" is Spanish for "the meadows" — a spring-fed oasis that was the only free-flowing water and grass for miles.
claims.nguon: Nevada Division of State Parks — Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort history
claims.trich_nguyen_van: With the only free-flowing water and grass for miles around, the site attracted the native Paiute as well as traders, emigrants and gold seekers traveling the Old Spanish Trail to California. The Spaniards called the place las vegas, which is Spanish for the meadows.

claims.claim_en: Rancher Helen J. Stewart sold her ranch — the land that became downtown Las Vegas — to the railroad in 1902.
claims.nguon: Nevada Division of State Parks — Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort history
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Helen Stewart successfully ran the ranch for nearly two decades until she sold the ranch and the land that would become downtown Las Vegas to the San Pedro, Los Angeles & Salt Lake Railroad in 1902.
claims.ghi_chu: Nguồn thứ cấp (UNLV/hồ sơ địa chính, qua WebSearch — CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC) nói chứng thư 08/12/1902 bán cho William A. Clark ($55.000), rồi chuyển cho công ty đường sắt 02/07/1903. Lời phim nên nói "sold ... in 1902" không nêu người mua cụ thể, hoặc "to Clark's railroad".

claims.claim_en: In the 1910 census, the whole of Clark County held just 3,321 people; the Las Vegas precinct, 945.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, Thirteenth Census (1910), Vol. III, Nevada, Table 1 (p. 78)
claims.ghi_chu: Trích là văn bản OCR của bản scan (lỗi "Connt:vi"; dòng Las Vegas bị OCR thành "045"). Đã đối chiếu bằng mắt trên ảnh trang 78 (pdf trang 65): "Clark County ... 3,321", "Las Vegas precinct ... 945". MÂU THUẪN: City timeline ghi "1910 Township population: 800" — dùng số Census.

claims.claim_en: Clark County was carved out of Lincoln County in 1909, making the railroad town a county seat.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, 1910 Census Vol. III (Nevada text)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Part of Lincoln County was taken in 1909 with those for the United States, as given in the to form Clark County.
claims.ghi_chu: City timeline: "Creation of the county government on July 1, 1909". PBS (thứ cấp) ghi 05/02/1908 — đó là ngày khác (luật?), không dùng.

claims.claim_en: In 1922, seven states split the Colorado River on paper: 7.5 million acre-feet a year for the Upper Basin, 7.5 million for the Lower.
claims.nguon: Colorado River Compact (1922), text via USBR
claims.trich_nguyen_van: (a) There is hereby apportioned from the Colorado River System in perpetuity to the Upper Basin and to the Lower Basin, respectively, the exclusive beneficial consumptive use of 7,500,000 acre-feet of water per annum,

claims.claim_en: The deal was struck in Santa Fe on November 24, 1922, with Commerce Secretary Herbert Hoover representing the United States.
claims.nguon: Colorado River Compact (1922), text via USBR
claims.trich_nguyen_van: who, after negotiations participated in by Herbert Hoover appointed by The President as the representative of the United States of America,
claims.ghi_chu: Văn bản Compact không gọi Hoover là "Secretary of Commerce"; chức danh này có trong Census story ("after becoming Secretary of Commerce in 1921"). Không nói "chaired".

claims.claim_en: The 1928 Boulder Canyon Project Act capped California at 4.4 million acre-feet and invited a deal giving Nevada 300,000.
claims.nguon: Boulder Canyon Project Act §4(a), 43 U.S.C. 617c (GPO GovInfo, 2023 ed.)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: there shall be apportioned to the State of Nevada 300,000 acre-feet and to the State of Arizona 2,800,000 acre-feet
claims.ghi_chu: "authorized to enter into an agreement" — hiệp định ba bang chưa từng ký; con số được Toà Tối cao xác lập năm 1963–1964 (xem N3).

claims.claim_en: Nevada's 300,000 acre-feet was fixed by the U.S. Supreme Court's 1964 decree in Arizona v. California.
claims.nguon: U.S. Supreme Court, Arizona v. California, Decree, 376 U.S. 340 (1964)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: 2,800,000 acre-feet for use in Arizona, 4,400,000 acre-feet for use in California, and 300,000 acre-feet for use in Nevada;

claims.claim_en: Nevada's negotiators thought 300,000 acre-feet was more than enough — Southern Nevada had no big farms and a tiny population.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Where your water comes from"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Nevada's share was 300,000 acre-feet per year. At the time, Nevada's negotiators felt this amount was more than enough. Southern Nevada had no significant agricultural or industrial users, groundwater seemed plentiful, and the area’s small population was not anticipated to grow significantly.

claims.claim_en: On March 19, 1931, Nevada re-legalized wide-open gambling when Governor Fred Balzar signed Assembly Bill 98.
claims.nguon: Nevada Legislative Counsel Bureau, Research Division, "Gaming in Nevada" Policy and Program Report (April 2016)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The supporters of Assembly Bill 98 (Chapter 99, Statutes of Nevada 1931) were victorious as it was passed by the Legislature (Senate vote: 13 to 3; Assembly vote: 24 to 1) and signed by Governor Fredrick B. Balzar on March 19, 1931.
claims.ghi_chu: "re-legalized": nguồn LCB đặt tiêu đề "The Relegalization of Gaming" (cờ bạc bị cấm từ 1909). Tên đầy đủ trong nguồn: "Fredrick B. Balzar".

claims.claim_en: That same year Nevada also shortened its divorce residency — two laws that shaped the image of Las Vegas.
claims.nguon: City of Las Vegas Timeline (CO-14073)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Nevada law legalized wide-open gambling and shortened the divorce residency. These changes laid the groundwork for industries that would define Las Vegas’s image in the years ahead.
claims.ghi_chu: Con số "six weeks" CHỈ có ở nguồn thứ cấp (luận án UNLV, báo) — CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC (cần Statutes of Nevada 1931). Lời phim dùng "shortened" là an toàn.

claims.claim_en: Work on the dam began in April 1931; the contractors had seven years — they poured the last concrete in May 1935.
claims.nguon: USBR Hoover Dam FAQ
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The contractors were allowed seven years from April 20, 1931, but concrete placement in the dam was completed May 29, 1935, and all features were completed by March 1, 1936.

toa_do.nguon: USBR accumweb.json, site Hoover Dam Powerplant (SDI 2070)

claims.claim_en: Six Companies won the dam contract on March 11, 1931, with a bid of $48,890,955.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, "History and the Census: Hoover Dam" (Sept 2025)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: On March 11, 1931, the federal government awarded the contract to Six Companies, Inc.—a joint venture of construction and engineering companies—which submitted a bid of $48,890,955.

claims.claim_en: In all, 21,000 men worked on the dam; at the peak in June 1934 there were 5,218 on a single day.
claims.nguon: USBR Hoover Dam FAQ
claims.trich_nguyen_van: A total of 21,000 men worked on the dam with an average of 3,500 and a maximum of 5,218 daily, which occurred in June 1934.

claims.claim_en: Officially, 96 men died building Hoover Dam.
claims.nguon: USBR, "Fatalities at Hoover Dam"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The "official" number of fatalities involved in building Hoover Dam is 96.
claims.ghi_chu: Phải kèm ý "official / industrial fatalities"; chết vì nắng nóng, viêm phổi không được tính (USBR nói rõ).

claims.claim_en: On September 30, 1935, President Franklin Roosevelt dedicated the dam — then officially called Boulder Dam.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, "History and the Census: Hoover Dam"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: On September 30, 1935, President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicated the Boulder Dam,
claims.ghi_chu: Census (1935) vs City of Las Vegas timeline ("completed and dedicated in 1936"). Hai nguồn chính quyền lệch; Census + nhiều nguồn khác thống nhất 30/09/1935 → dùng 1935, ghi chú lỗi của City timeline.

toa_do.nguon: USBR accumweb.json, site Hoover Dam Powerplant (SDI 2070)

claims.claim_en: The reservoir behind it began filling on February 1, 1935, and was named for Reclamation Commissioner Elwood Mead.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, "History and the Census: Hoover Dam"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Engineers began filling Lake Mead—named for Elwood Mead , commissioner of the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation—on February 1, 1935.
claims.ghi_chu: Dữ liệu HDB USBR bắt đầu 02/02/1935 ở 670 ft — khớp.

claims.claim_en: The name changed twice: Hoover Dam in 1930, Boulder Dam under Roosevelt, and Hoover Dam again by act of Congress in 1947.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, "History and the Census: Hoover Dam"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: During a September 17, 1930, groundbreaking ceremony, Secretary of the Interior Ray Lyman Wilbur renamed it Hoover Dam

claims.claim_en: Between 1941 and 1942, four big hotel-casinos opened, including El Rancho Vegas and the Last Frontier on what became the Strip.
claims.nguon: City of Las Vegas Timeline (CO-14073)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Between 1941 and 1942, four major hotel-casinos opened that defined new Las Vegas hospitality: El Cortez on Fremont Street, Nevada Biltmore on North Main Street, and El Rancho Vegas and Hotel Last Frontier on The Strip south of the city limits.

claims.claim_en: Clark County grew from 16,414 people in 1940 to 127,016 in 1960 — almost eightfold in twenty years.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, 1990 CPH-2-30 Nevada, Table 3 (Population 1940–1990)

toa_do.nguon: Census 2020 PL 94-171 geo header, Clark County internal point (không phải vị trí El Rancho Vegas)

claims.claim_en: The city of Las Vegas itself went from 8,422 residents in 1940 to 64,405 in 1960.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau, 1960 Census, Number of Inhabitants, Nevada, Table 5
claims.ghi_chu: Bản scan; đọc bằng mắt từ ảnh render (pdftoppm 220 dpi). Số 1950 (24,624) khớp văn bản OCR của 1950 Census (census1950_v1_nevada.txt).

claims.claim_en: The Flamingo opened on December 26, 1946.
claims.nguon: Chỉ nguồn thứ cấp (Wikipedia, History.com) qua WebSearch
claims.trich_nguyen_van: KHÔNG có trích nguyên văn từ nguồn chính quyền trong phiên này.
claims.ghi_chu: Mốc M4 đã có C22–C24 XÁC MINH; claim này chỉ để tham khảo. Bugsy Siegel = nhân vật tội phạm, tránh sa đà.

claims.claim_en: In June 1971, Lake Mead water began flowing to the Las Vegas Valley through the Southern Nevada Water Project's first stage.
claims.nguon: USBR, Robert B. Griffith Water Project
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The first water deliveries were made to the Las Vegas Valley District on June 16, 1971, and the first stage became operational on November 1 that year.
claims.ghi_chu: City timeline (1954) nói đường ống LVVWD "linking the city to Lake Mead’s water for the first time" — nghĩa là đã có nước Lake Mead từ 1950s qua hệ thống BMI/Henderson; lời phim nên nói "a direct pipeline" (City) hoặc "the Southern Nevada Water Project" để tránh mâu thuẫn.

toa_do.nguon: USBR accumweb.json, site "SNWA Diversion" (dữ liệu ghi 114.8 không dấu; kinh độ Tây)

claims.claim_en: Until the early 1970s, the valley lived mostly on local groundwater.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Where your water comes from"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Our community relied on local groundwater supplies to meet most of its water needs until the early 1970s, when facilities to treat and deliver Colorado River water were constructed.

claims.claim_en: The Southern Nevada Water Authority was created on July 25, 1991.
claims.nguon: Nevada Legislature, AB 356 (2021), Sec. 38 (enrolled)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: “Southern Nevada Water Authority” means the political subdivision of the State of Nevada created on July 25, 1991,

claims.claim_en: Today about 90 percent of Southern Nevada’s water comes from the Colorado River, drawn from Lake Mead.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Where your water comes from"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Southern Nevada gets about 90 percent of its water supply from the Colorado River,

claims.claim_en: In 2025 Nevada consumed 197,570 acre-feet of Colorado River water — well under its 300,000 — while diverting more than twice that and returning the rest.
claims.nguon: USBR, Colorado River Accounting and Water Use Report: Arizona, California, and Nevada, CY2025 (Table 1, Table 6)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Nevada 197,570 Total Lower Division States Consumptive Use
claims.ghi_chu: Bảng 6: diversion 443.525 af; measured returns 244.412 af; consumptive 197.570 af. Năm 2025 Nevada còn bị cắt 13.000 (shortage) và tạo 89.430 af System Conservation (SNWA). 2024: 212.428 af (decree2024).

claims.claim_en: Return-flow credits: every gallon of treated wastewater sent back to Lake Mead lets Southern Nevada take another gallon out.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Where your water comes from"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Every gallon of water that is returned to the Colorado River through return-flow credits allows Southern Nevada to take another gallon out, which stretches our limited water supply.

claims.claim_en: Per-person water use in Southern Nevada fell 58 percent between 2002 and 2025, while the population grew by about 876,000.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Conservation initiatives"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Conservation efforts have helped the community reduce its per capita water use by 58 percent between 2002 and 2025, even as the population increased by approximately 876,000 residents during that time.
claims.ghi_chu: Chỉ dùng tỷ lệ % của SNWA. Số GPCD tuyệt đối mâu thuẫn theo định nghĩa: 211→89 GPCD (consumptive, Nevada Independent 30/09/2026, thứ cấp); EPA fact sheet 314 (2003) → 205 (2014) (tổng cầu, thứ cấp); Mulroy 2013 trước Thượng viện "net water use of 75 gpcd" (C53). Không đưa con số "314 (2002)" vào lời phim.

claims.claim_en: Lake Mead's previous record low came on July 28, 2022: 1,040.58 feet above sea level.
claims.nguon: USBR HDB (lchdb, SDI 1930, Lake Mead end-of-day elevation)
claims.ghi_chu: Cuối tháng 07/2022 (bảng mead-elv): 1.040,92 ft — khác số ngày thấp nhất; nói rõ "daily low".

claims.claim_en: Southern Nevada built a third intake deep in Lake Mead; it began delivering water in September 2015.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Intake 3 & Low Lake Level Pumping Station"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Intake 3 began conveying water to our water treatment facilities in September 2015.

claims.claim_en: A low-lake-level pumping station, finished in 2020, switched on in April 2022 when the lake fell too far for an older intake.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Intake 3 & Low Lake Level Pumping Station"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Completed in 2020, the Low Lake Level Pumping Station started operating in April 2022 when the dramatic drop in the elevation of Lake Mead rendered one of our community's primary intake pumping stations inoperable.
claims.ghi_chu: Cùng trang: tiếp cận nước dưới "dead pool" 895 ft. Không dùng con số "875 ft" (không có trong nguồn).

claims.claim_en: Since 1999, Southern Nevadans have torn out 250 million square feet of grass for rebates.
claims.nguon: SNWA, "Conservation initiatives"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Water Smart Landscape Rebate Program - 250 million square feet of grass have been removed, saving 203 billion gallons of water since 1999.

claims.claim_en: Starting January 1, 2027, Colorado River water may no longer irrigate "nonfunctional" grass in Southern Nevada outside single-family homes.
claims.nguon: Nevada Legislature, AB 356 (81st Session, 2021), Sec. 39 (enrolled)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Sec. 39. 1. Except as otherwise provided in this section, on and after January 1, 2027, the waters of the Colorado River distributed by the Southern Nevada Water Authority or one of the member agencies of the Southern Nevada Water Authority may not be used to irrigate nonfunctional turf on any property that is not zoned exclusively for a single-family residence.
claims.ghi_chu: Bản Special Acts hiện hành (rev. 2025) đổi chữ thành "not used exclusively as a single-family residence" — luật đã được sửa sau 2021; khi lồng tiếng nói "outside single-family homes".

claims.claim_en: On August 21, 2026, with the seven states still deadlocked, the Interior Department imposed a ten-year framework and two years of rules.
claims.nguon: DOI ROD (Aug 2026) + USBR news release 21/08/2026
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Despite these efforts, the seven Basin States were unable to reach an agreement.

claims.claim_en: For 2027, Nevada’s share drops to 250,000 acre-feet — a 50,000 acre-foot cut; Arizona loses 760,000 and California 440,000.
claims.nguon: DOI, 2027–2028 Operating Guidelines §5.3.A.2
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Of the 6.25 maf that shall be apportioned each calendar year for consumptive use in the Lower Division States of which 2.04 maf shall be apportioned for use in Arizona, 3.96 maf shall be apportioned for use in California and 250,000 acre-feet (af) shall be apportioned for use in Nevada, reflecting reductions of 760,000 af in Arizona, 440,000 af in California, and 50,000 af in Nevada, in accordance with a Lower Basin implementing agreement(s).
claims.ghi_chu: Phân chia giữa các bang là "if the Lower Basin States implement their proposed sharing agreement" (nr5392); nếu không, Bộ trưởng tự quyết theo luật. Claim "California's first water cut in history" (tiêu đề video) CHƯA có nguồn chính quyền nói "first" — không dùng.

claims.claim_en: In August 2026 Lake Mead sank below its 2022 record — and kept falling, to 1,037.54 feet by October 14.
claims.nguon: USBR HDB (lchdb, SDI 1930)
claims.ghi_chu: Ngày cuối 1.037,54 ft (14/10/2026) có trong cùng tệp. P kiểm lại tệp HDB (15/10): lần cuối hồ thấp hơn 1.037,54 ft là 21/04/1937 (1.037,45 ft) khi hồ còn đang tích nước lần đầu → nói "the lowest since the lake was first filling in 1937" hoặc "lowest since the lake first filled"; KHÔNG nói "lowest ever".

claims.claim_en: Upstream, Lake Powell hit its own record low: 3,516.62 feet on September 15, 2026.
claims.nguon: USBR HDB (uchdb2, SDI 1928, Lake Powell)

claims.claim_en: The winter of 2025–26 brought the lowest snowpack ever observed in the basin.
claims.nguon: DOI ROD (Aug 2026), Introduction
claims.trich_nguyen_van: partially a result of the lowest observed snowpack on record during the winter of 2025–2026.

claims.claim_en: By July, Reclamation expected just 36 percent of average inflow into Lake Powell for water year 2026 — and only 17 percent for the April-to-July runoff.
claims.nguon: USBR, July 2026 Most Probable 24-Month Study (15/07/2026)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The 2026 April through July unregulated inflow forecast for Lake Powell is 1.08 maf or 17% of average. The WY 2026 unregulated inflow forecast for Lake Powell is 3.50 maf or 36% of average.
claims.ghi_chu: Dự báo dòng chảy do NWS Colorado Basin River Forecast Center cung cấp (cùng trang).

claims.claim_en: Three days after the decision, Nevada and the Southern Nevada Water Authority sued the Interior Department in federal court.
claims.nguon: U.S. District Court D. Nev., Complaint, Case 2:26-cv-02665 (filed 08/24/26); Office of Governor Lombardo press release 24/08/2026
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Case 2:26-cv-02665 Document 1 Filed 08/24/26
claims.ghi_chu: Tệp đơn kiện lấy qua 8newsnow.com (bản PDF có header PACER) — là bản sao do báo đăng; nên tải lại từ PACER/CourtListener để có bản gốc toà. Chưa có phán quyết.

claims.claim_en: Mexico, too, agreed to take 250,000 acre-feet less each year in 2027 and 2028.
claims.nguon: IBWC press release 09/09/2026 (Minute 334)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Colorado River water deliveries to Mexico will be reduced by 250,000 acre-feet (308,372,250 cubic meters) per year during the same period.

claims.claim_en: In October, the remnants of Hurricane Rachel swept right over Lake Mead — and the lake rose just six hundredths of a foot.
claims.nguon: NOAA/NWS National Hurricane Center, Remnants of Rachel Advisory 58 (11/10/2026); USBR HDB
claims.trich_nguyen_van: At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the remnants of Rachel were located near latitude 35.8 North, longitude 114.6 West.
claims.ghi_chu: Mực hồ: 10/10/2026 = 1.037,65; 11/10/2026 = 1.037,71 (+0,06 ft); 12/10 = 1.037,65 (HDB). Tiêu đề video gọi "Tropical Storm Rachel ~13/10" — NHC: hệ thống là "Hurricane RACHEL" (EP18), advisory cuối 11/10/2026 dạng tàn dư. Thiệt hại lũ ở Las Vegas: CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC (NWS Las Vegas).

claims.claim_en: In 2025 one California farm district — Imperial Irrigation District — consumed 2.19 million acre-feet, about eleven times all of Nevada.
claims.nguon: USBR CY2025 Water Accounting Report, Table (California) "Total IID Consumptive Use"
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Total IID Consumptive Use
claims.ghi_chu: Giá trị tổng (cột TOTAL) = 2.187.165 af; Nevada 197.570 af → 11,07 lần. Trích chỉ là nhãn dòng vì bảng nhiều cột; số đọc từ cùng dòng của tệp text (cột cuối). Không dùng "quyền 3,1 triệu" (QSA) — chưa có nguồn gốc trong phiên.

claims.claim_en: Yet Imperial County is poorer: 18.8 percent of residents lived in poverty in 2024, against 12.5 percent in Clark County.
claims.nguon: U.S. Census Bureau SAIPE 2024 (est24all.txt, phát hành 07/01/2026)
claims.ghi_chu: Dòng Imperial: poverty all ages 18.8% (KTC 90%: 16.3–21.3), median household income $60,477. Clark: 12.5%, $80,047. US: 12.1%, $81,604. Thất nghiệp Imperial (CA EDD LAUS) BỊ CHẶN: lỗi chứng chỉ TLS của labormarketinfo.edd.ca.gov; bls.gov 403.

claims.claim_en: Downstream, the Colorado River Indian Tribes hold decreed rights to as much as 719,248 acre-feet of diversions a year — more than double Nevada’s share.
claims.nguon: U.S. Supreme Court, Arizona v. California, Consolidated Decree, 547 U.S. 150 (2006), Art. II(D)(4)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: (4) The Colorado River Indian Reservation in annual quantities not to exceed (i) 719,248 acre-feet of diver sions from the mainstream or (ii) the quantity of main stream water necessary to supply the consumptive use required for irrigation of 107,903 acres and for the satis faction of related uses, whichever of (i) or (ii) is less,
claims.ghi_chu: CY2025: CRIT consumptive use 326.094 af (decree2025) > Nevada 197.570. Nói "decreed rights", không ngụ ý "lãng phí"; quyền ưu tiên 1865 có trước Las Vegas.

claims.claim_en: On the Navajo Nation, whose western boundary runs along the Colorado, members use around seven gallons of water a day for all household needs, according to the case record cited at the Supreme Court.
claims.nguon: U.S. Supreme Court, Arizona v. Navajo Nation, 599 U.S. ___ (2023), Gorsuch, J., dissenting (trích hồ sơ App. 101)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: “Mem- bers of the Navajo Nation use around 7 gallons of water per day for all of their household needs”
claims.ghi_chu: Đây là trích dẫn hồ sơ trong Ý KIẾN BẤT ĐỒNG, không phải phán quyết của đa số. Cách nói an toàn: "according to the record cited by the dissent". Không dựng hình ảnh khắc hoạ người Navajo khi chưa có tư vấn văn hoá.

claims.claim_en: In 2014, a deliberate pulse of about 105,000 acre-feet reconnected the Colorado River to its estuary in Mexico for the first time since 2001.
claims.nguon: IBWC, Minute 319 Colorado River Limitrophe and Delta Environmental Flows Monitoring, Final Report (2018)
claims.trich_nguyen_van: The pulse flow achieved lateral and longitudinal connectivity along the entire river from Morelos Dam to the estuary for the first time since 2001.
claims.ghi_chu: Báo cáo nói "estuary" (vùng nghiên cứu kéo tới Upper Gulf of California); không nói "reached the sea".

claims.claim_en: Water manager John Entsminger warned the Senate in 2022 that "a slow-motion train wreck for 20 years is accelerating."
claims.nguon: Statement of John J. Entsminger, Senate Energy & Natural Resources Committee, 14/06/2022
claims.trich_nguyen_van: What has been a slow-motion train wreck for 20 years is accelerating, and the moment of reckoning is near.

claims.claim_en: His predecessor Pat Mulroy told senators in 2013 that after two years of drought, Las Vegas went from a reliable 50-year plan to facing "immediate severe and debilitating shortages."
claims.nguon: Statement of Patricia Mulroy, Senate Energy & Natural Resources Committee, 25/04/2013
claims.trich_nguyen_van: In 2002, after only 2 years of this now-13- year drought, we went from having a reliable 50-year plan to facing a reality of immediate severe and debilitating shortages.
claims.ghi_chu: Cùng văn bản: "a net water use of 75 gpcd in the driest city in America" — MÂU THUẪN về định nghĩa với số SNWA (xem C32); không dùng. Nhiệm kỳ GM (1989/1991–2014) CHỜ XÁC MINH GỐC.

claims.claim_en: Nevada's governor said the community used slightly less than 212,500 acre-feet in 2024 — and could be left with less than 86,500.
claims.nguon: Office of Governor Joe Lombardo, press release 24/08/2026
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Specifically, Nevada stands to have its 300,000-acre-foot allocation cut by up to 213,556 acre-feet, leaving Las Vegas and surrounding cities less than 86,500 acre-feet per year. For context, the community used slightly less than 212,500 acre-feet of water in 2024.
claims.ghi_chu: Là lập luận của một bên đương sự (kịch bản xấu nhất theo sideboard 3,0 maf), không phải mức cắt 2027 (50.000 af). Số 2024 khớp USBR: 212.428 af.

claims.claim_en: Every year Lake Mead loses twice as much water to evaporation as Nevada uses, Entsminger testified.
claims.nguon: Statement of John J. Entsminger, Senate ENR, 14/06/2022
claims.trich_nguyen_van: Lake Mead loses twice as much water to evaporation than we use each year.
claims.ghi_chu: Trích nguyên văn có, nhưng là số tự khai của SNWA; cần đối chiếu số bốc hơi Lake Mead (accumweb.json SDI 1776 / Decree report) trước khi dùng như sự thật.

claims.claim_en: In 2026 the Lower Basin was still in shortage: Nevada was apportioned 287,000 acre-feet instead of 300,000.
claims.nguon: USBR 2026 Annual Operating Plan + 2007 Interim Guidelines ROD §2.D.1.a
claims.trich_nguyen_van: which 2.48 maf shall be apportioned for use in Arizona and 287,000 af shall be apportioned for use in Nevada
claims.ghi_chu: AOP 2026: Shortage Condition 2.D.1.a (Lake Mead dự báo 01/01/2026 = 1.055,88 ft) + DCP contribution của Nevada (số 2026 không ghi trong AOP; năm 2025 là 8.000 af). "fifth straight": SNWA nói "Shortage conditions have remained in effect since 2022" → 2022–2026 = 5 năm (suy luận, kiểm lại khi viết).
